defect.summary: The F2a extension_predicate is under-frozen on three axes: (1) the manifold category of M', (2) the differentiability class of the embedding iota, (3) the interior-future requirement of clause (f). The F2b (C0) sibling at b2ab6acb froze all three (clause (c) SMOOTH M'; witness_type C-infinity iota; clause (f) int(M'-iota(M)) non-empty and p in int(...)). The C2 class therefore quantifies over an extension class that is reader-dependent while its C0 sibling is exact.

defect.class_boundary_note: This repair sharpens a definition (extension predicate), not a conclusion. The class token stays C2, frozen_regularity stays C2, the equation requirement stays classical_ricci, and the conclusion_type is not touched. The template is the accepted F2b F2b-16-03 smooth-category repair, which is the sibling-class precedent at the same gate.

recommendation: Option A (sibling-aligned smooth category) on every site. Option B is recorded per site as a fallback and is sufficient for a C2 metric in isolation, but it would leave F2a and F2b in different manifold categories and is therefore not the uniform choice.

sites.old_text: (a) iota: M -> M' is an isometric embedding (iota_* g = g' restricted to iota(M));
sites.new_text: (a) iota: M -> M' is a C-infinity isometric embedding (iota_* g = g' restricted to iota(M)); the differentiability class of iota is frozen here and is not left to convention [sibling precedent: F2b falsifier.tier_1.witness_type freezes a C-infinity isometric embedding iota];

alternatives.new_text: (a) iota: M -> M' is a C2 isometric embedding (iota_* g = g' restricted to iota(M)); the differentiability class of iota is frozen here and is not left to convention;
alternatives.note: C2 is the minimal class for iota_* g' to be C2 when g' is C2, so option B is internally sufficient, but it does not match the F2b witness_type token.

sites.rationale: F2a clause (d) requires g' of class C2, so iota must be at least C2 for iota_* g = g' to be evaluated. Naming C-infinity matches the sibling and the smooth category of M and M'.

sites.old_text: (c) M' is connected and time-orientable, and its time orientation restricts to that of M;
sites.new_text: (c) M' is a SMOOTH (C-infinity) connected 4-manifold, time-orientable, and its time orientation restricts to that of M; the smooth structure is the category in which the metric is a tensor field, while the metric itself is only C2 [sibling precedent: F2b clause (c), worker-16 F2b-16-03 accepted];

alternatives.new_text: (c) M' is a C2 connected 4-manifold, time-orientable, and its time orientation restricts to that of M; the C2 structure is the category in which the metric is a tensor field;
alternatives.note: C2 category is sufficient for a C2 metric but differs from the frozen F2b category.

sites.rationale: Clause (d) already speaks of a C2 metric on M'; a bare topological 4-manifold cannot carry a classical tensor field. The F2b repair froze SMOOTH as the category and separated it from the metric regularity; F2a must not leave the category to convention while its sibling does not.
sites.precedent: schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml#b2ab6acb2bbe:91 (clause (c) SMOOTH (C-infinity) connected 4-manifold with worker-16 F2b-16-03 rationale)

sites.old_text: (f) the extension adds points to the future: there exist q in iota(M) and p in M' minus iota(M) with p in I^+(q; g').
sites.new_text: (f) the extension adds interior points to the future: int(M' minus iota(M)) is non-empty AND there exist q in iota(M) and p in int(M' minus iota(M)) with p in I^+(q; g'), where I^+ is the chronological future. The interior requirement blocks an extension that only adds boundary or dense-open points [sibling precedent: F2b clause (f), R2 major accepted]. For a C2 metric the chronological future is open and does not depend on the curve class, so the C0 convention caveat in the sibling does not apply here;
sites.rationale: At the pin, p is only required to lie in M' minus iota(M), which can include boundary-only or dense-open additions; the F2b sibling closed exactly this escape with int(M' minus iota(M)) non-empty and p in the interior. The C2 class has a well-defined open chronological future, so the sibling's degenerate-causality caveat drops out rather than being copied.
sites.precedent: schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml#b2ab6acb2bbe:94 (clause (f) interior requirement, R2 major: clause (f) was escapable)

sites.old_text: extension_topology: "M' is a connected 4-manifold containing iota(M) as an open proper subset; M' is NOT assumed globally hyperbolic, compact, or AF"
sites.new_text: extension_topology: "M' is a connected SMOOTH 4-manifold (the category in which the C2 metric is a tensor field) containing iota(M) as an open proper subset; the metric g' is only C2. M' is NOT assumed globally hyperbolic, compact, or AF. The smooth category is frozen here and is not left to convention [sibling precedent: F2b extension_topology]."

alternatives.new_text: extension_topology: "M' is a connected C2 4-manifold (the category in which the C2 metric is a tensor field) containing iota(M) as an open proper subset; the metric g' is only C2. M' is NOT assumed globally hyperbolic, compact, or AF."
alternatives.note: C2 category consistent with option B on S2; not uniform with F2b.

sites.rationale: The manifold category must be frozen in the topology block as well as the predicate, because the topology block is what a machine consumer reads for M' and it currently just says '4-manifold'.

sites.old_text: witness_type: "an open (or at least non-meager) set of one-ended AF vacuum data whose maximal developments admit proper future C2 vacuum extensions, with the extension exhibited (an explicit family, not a numerical near-solution)"
sites.new_text: witness_type: "an open (or at least non-meager) set of one-ended AF vacuum data whose maximal developments admit proper future C2 vacuum extensions, with the extension exhibited explicitly (SMOOTH 4-manifold M', C2 nondegenerate Lorentzian metric g', C-infinity isometric embedding iota, an interior future point added as in clause (f); an explicit family, not a numerical near-solution)"
sites.rationale: A falsifier must exhibit a witness in the same frozen class it refutes. At the pin the witness_type does not name the category of M' or the class of iota, so a machine-checked witness would be under-specified in exactly the same three axes as the predicate.
